mainTopic: A כהן's מנחת חוטא: what happens to its remainder, where we learn that a כהן may serve on his own offering, and how the פסוק "כליל תהיה לא תאכל" is read.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about a כהן's מנחת חוטא. Like a ישראל's, it has a קומץ removed. But from the פסוק "לכהן כמנחה" we learn that the remainder is not eaten: the קומץ and the שירים are each burned on their own. The גמרא then asks why we need this פסוק to teach that a כהן may serve on his own offering. Its answer is that each of three פסוקים teaches something the others cannot, and the last case is a deliberate false oath. Next comes another ברייתא: רבי שמעון says the שירים are burned, while his son רבי אלעזר says they are scattered on the בית הדשן. רבי יוחנן questions this, and רבי אבא suggests the שירים are simply wasted. A teaching about the פסוק "כל מנחת כהן כליל תהיה לא תאכל" supports that idea, and אביי and רבא argue over how to split the פסוק between the כהן's נדבה and his חובה. The רבנן use the same פסוק for a גזירה שוה on "כליל", which gives both the חביתין and the priest's מנחה both rules. The amud ends as רבינא begins asking about a כהן who eats from the אימורין, a question that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A priest's sinner meal offering has a handful removed, like an Israelite's
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא compares a כהן's מנחת חוטא to a ישראל's. Just as a handful is removed from the ישראל's, a handful is also removed from the כהן's.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sinner's meal offering of כהנים is like the sinner's meal offering of a ישראל. Just as a handful is taken from the ישראל's, a handful is also taken from the כהנים's.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states a comparison: a כהן's מנחת חוטא is treated like a ישראל's, so a handful (קמיצה) is removed from it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא builds a "just as… so too" (מה… אף) comparison between the two offerings. The one thing it applies so far is קמיצה: both get a handful removed.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal offering brought by a sinner who cannot afford an animal or birds
A handful (קוֹמֶץ) is removed from it
Priests and regular Jews who are not כהנים
"Just as… so too": a comparison formula

phrases.english: The meal offering of a sinner brought by priests
is like the meal offering of a sinner brought by an Israelite.

phrases.aramaic: מָה מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְמֶצֶת,
phrases.english: Just as the meal offering of a sinner of an Israelite has a handful removed,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים נִקְמֶצֶת.
phrases.english: so too the meal offering of a sinner of priests has a handful removed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים כְּמִנְחַת חוֹטֵא שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that started before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן's מנחת חוטא has קמיצה, just like a ישראל's.

steps.title: Should the priest's remainder also be eaten?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא pushes its own comparison further. If the offerings are alike, then the כהן's remainder should be eaten just like the ישראל's.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, just as the ישראל's offering has a handful removed and the rest is eaten, the כהן's should also have a handful removed and the rest eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges itself. If the comparison is complete, the כהן's leftover flour should be eaten too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל's מנחה has two parts: the קומץ goes on the altar and the שיריים are eaten by כהנים. The challenge asks whether the comparison carries over the eating part as well, not just the קמיצה.

keyTerms.meaning: "If so, then just as…": pushing a comparison further to test it
Its remainder: the flour left after the handful is removed
Are eaten (by the כהנים)

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: If so, then just as the meal offering of a sinner of an Israelite
has a handful removed and its remainder is eaten,
so too the meal offering of a sinner of priests
should have a handful removed and its remainder eaten?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the comparison in step 1 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between a כהן's and a ישראל's מנחת חוטא (step 1).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two offerings are fully alike, the eating of the שיריים should carry over too.

steps.title: The verse limits the comparison: the remainder is burned separately
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "לכהן כמנחה" teaches that the offerings are alike only in part. The כהן's handful is burned by itself, and the remainder is also burned by itself instead of being eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "to the כהן, like the מנחה." It is like the מנחה regarding the כהן's service, but not like the מנחה regarding the altar fires. How does this work? The handful is offered on its own, and the remainder is offered on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from a פסוק. The כהן's offering is like a ישראל's in having a קומץ, but the rest is not eaten. It is also burned on the altar, separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads "לכהן כמנחה" as a limited comparison. The offerings are alike in the כהן's handling of the קמיצה, but different in what happens with the אשים, the altar fire. So the קומץ is burned alone, and then the שיריים are burned alone, instead of being eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse teaches": introduces the פסוק that settles the question
The fires of the altar
"How so?": asks how two ideas fit together
Offered by itself: burned on the altar separately

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן's מנחת חוטא has קמיצה like a ישראל's. But nothing is eaten: the קומץ is burned by itself, and the שיריים are burned by themselves.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the כהן gets to eat the remainder because the פסוק says "לכהן." Here the ברייתא reads the word as a comparison about the service, and the remainder is burned, not eaten.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse states: "The priest's, as the meal offering."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:13

phrases.english: Regarding the priest, it is like the meal offering,
but regarding the fires, it is not like the meal offering.
How is this?
The handful is sacrificed by itself,
and the remainder is sacrificed by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A verse limits the scope of the comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן's remainder would be eaten like a ישראל's.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קומץ is burned by itself and the שיריים are burned by themselves. Nothing is eaten.

steps.title: Is the rule that a priest may serve his own offering learned from here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question. Is the law that a כהן's own service on his offering is valid really learned from this פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: This law, that the service of the offering is valid when he does it himself: is it learned from here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new issue and asks whether this פסוק is really the source for letting a כהן do the service of his own offering. This sets up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the ברייתא, the פסוק "לכהן כמנחה" was used to teach that a כהן may do the service of his own מנחת חוטא. The question "מהכא נפקא?" suggests the גמרא suspects the rule comes from a different source. It will look into that next.

keyTerms.meaning: Its service: the Temple rites done with the offering
Valid when done by him, the owner-כהן himself
"Is it derived from here?": questioning the source of a law

phrases.english: This law, that its service is valid when performed by him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the כהן who brought the offering, doing the service on his own מנחה.

phrases.english: is it derived from here?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא שֶׁתְּהֵא עֲבוֹדָתָהּ כְּשֵׁרָה בּוֹ מֵהָכָא נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא's ruling to questioning the source of a related law.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using "לכהן כמנחה" as the source that a כהן's service on his own offering is valid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The question suggests this law may come from a different source, which would make this derivation unnecessary.

steps.title: Another verse already lets a כהן bring his offerings whenever he wants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns from a פסוק in דברים that a כהן may come and bring his own offerings at any time.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from there: From where do we know that a כהן may come and bring his offerings at any time and any hour he wants? The פסוק says: 'And he comes with all the desire of his soul, and he shall serve.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question from step 4 by pointing to a different source. A ברייתא already learns from a פסוק in דברים that a כהן may bring his own offerings whenever he wants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a כהן may serve on his own offerings at any time, it seems we already know he may serve on his own offering. So why do we need the פסוק about the מנחת חוטא for this?

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from there (from a different source)
The desire of his soul (whenever he wants)
At any time and at any hour

phrases.english: It is learned from there:
From where do we know regarding a priest
that he comes and offers his own offerings
at any time and at any hour that he wants?
The verse says:
"And he comes with all the desire of his soul, and he shall serve."
phrases.notes: דברים 18:6–7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the question of step 4 by naming the other source.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the פסוק of the כהן's מנחת חוטא to teach that a כהן may serve on his own offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק in דברים already teaches that a כהן may bring his own offerings at any time, so the first פסוק seems unneeded for this.

steps.title: The verse in דברים covers only offerings not brought for a sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that from the פסוק in דברים we would think this applies only to offerings not brought for a sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were only from there, I would have said: this applies only to something not brought for a sin, but something brought for a sin, I would say not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק in דברים is not enough. It might only allow a כהן to serve on offerings that are not brought for a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים talks about a כהן coming 'with all the desire of his soul,' which sounds like an offering he wants to bring. A מנחת חוטא is brought because of a sin, so we need the פסוק about it to teach that a כהן may serve on that kind of offering too.

keyTerms.meaning: If it were only from there
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
This applies only to...
Something (an offering) brought for a sin

phrases.english: If it were from there, I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי – דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בָּא עַל חֵטְא,
phrases.english: this applies only to something that does not come for a sin,
but something that does come for a sin –
I would say no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the other source: each פסוק teaches something the other cannot.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the פסוק in דברים alone, a כהן could serve only on offerings not brought for a sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק of the מנחת חוטא teaches that a כהן may serve on his own offering even when it comes for a sin.

steps.title: A verse in במדבר already teaches a כהן can atone for himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again: a פסוק in במדבר already teaches that a כהן can bring about his own atonement, even for a sin offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is this also learned from here? It is learned from there: 'And the כהן shall atone for the soul that sins accidentally, when he sins accidentally.' This teaches that the כהן can be atoned for through himself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question on the answer of step 6. Even for an offering brought for a sin, another פסוק already teaches that a כהן may atone for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said we need the מנחת חוטא פסוק for sin offerings. Now the גמרא shows a פסוק in במדבר that already covers sin offerings, so the question comes back: why do we need the מנחת חוטא פסוק?

keyTerms.meaning: And is this also...?
And he shall atone
This teaches
Gets atonement through himself (doing his own service)

phrases.english: But is this also learned from here?
phrases.notes: "This" means a כהן serving on his own sin offering; "here" is the פסוק of the מנחת חוטא.

phrases.english: It is learned from there:
"And the priest shall atone for the soul
that sins accidentally, when he sins accidentally,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:28

phrases.english: this teaches that the priest gets atonement
through himself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 6 that the מנחת חוטא פסוק is needed for offerings brought for a sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק in במדבר already teaches that a כהן can atone for himself for a sin, so the מנחת חוטא פסוק still seems unneeded.

steps.title: The verse in במדבר covers only an accidental sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that from the פסוק in במדבר we would think this applies only to an accidental sin, not a deliberate one. The מנחת חוטא פסוק teaches otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were from that one, I would have said: this applies only to an accidental sin, but for a deliberate sin, no. So the פסוק teaches us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק in במדבר only speaks about an accidental sin. The מנחת חוטא פסוק is needed to teach that a כהן may serve on his own offering even when it was for a deliberate sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in במדבר says 'שגגה' (by accident) twice, so it could be limited to accidental sins. The מנחת חוטא פסוק adds the case of a deliberate sin. Now each of the three פסוקים has its own job.

keyTerms.meaning: By accident
On purpose, deliberately
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.whatToRemember: Three פסוקים, three jobs: דברים — a כהן may bring his own offerings any time; במדבר — even a sin offering, for an accidental sin; the מנחת חוטא פסוק — even for a deliberate sin.

phrases.english: If it were from that one, I would have said:
this applies only to an accidental sin,
but for a deliberate sin – no,
so it teaches us.
phrases.notes: "It" is the פסוק of the כהן's מנחת חוטא, which teaches that even a deliberate sin is included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the other source: the פסוק in במדבר covers only accidental sins.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the פסוק in במדבר alone, a כהן could atone for himself only for an accidental sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק of the מנחת חוטא teaches that a כהן may serve on his own offering even for a deliberate sin.

steps.title: How can a deliberate sin bring a sin offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a case where a deliberate sinner brings a מנחת חוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A deliberate sin: how can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: In Step 8 the גמרא said the מנחת חוטא פסוק teaches about a deliberate sin. Now it asks for a real example, because sin offerings usually come only for accidental sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a קרבן atones only for a sin done by accident (שוגג), not on purpose. So the claim from Step 8 needs a real case to stand on. This question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: On purpose, deliberately
How can you find it? (asking for a real case)

phrases.english: For a deliberate sin, how can you find it?
phrases.notes: He means: when would someone who sinned on purpose ever bring a מנחת חוטא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a real case behind the answer given in Step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where a deliberate sinner brings a מנחת חוטא

steps.title: The case is a deliberate false oath
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a deliberate false oath is atoned for with a קרבן, which can be a מנחת חוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the case of a deliberate false oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the case is a false oath sworn on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A false oath is one of the special sins where a קרבן is brought even if it was done on purpose. A poor person brings it as a מנחה, so a כהן could bring a מנחת חוטא for a deliberate sin. This keeps Step 8's answer standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Swearing a false oath on purpose

steps.whatToRemember: A deliberate false oath is a case where even a deliberate sinner brings a קרבן, so the מנחת חוטא פסוק can teach about a deliberate sin.

phrases.english: In a deliberate oath.
phrases.notes: Someone who knowingly swore falsely. Even though he did it on purpose, he still brings a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A deliberate false oath, which is atoned for with a קרבן even when done on purpose

steps.title: What happens to a כהן's מנחת חוטא: father and son disagree
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: רבי שמעון says the קומץ and the שירים are each burned on their own. רבי אלעזר says the שירים are scattered on the בית הדשן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in another ברייתא: רבי שמעון says a כהן's מנחת חוטא has a handful taken. The handful is burned by itself, and the rest is burned by itself. רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says: the handful is burned by itself, and the rest is scattered on the place of the ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings a ברייתא with a disagreement about what to do with the leftover part of a כהן's מנחת חוטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually after the קומץ is burned, the כהנים eat the שירים. But a כהן's own מנחה is not eaten, so something else must be done with the rest. רבי שמעון says it is burned separately on the מזבח, while his son says it is scattered on the בית הדשן.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour burned on the מזבח
The leftover part of the מנחה after the קומץ is removed
The place where ashes are put

phrases.english: It was taught in another ברייתא: רבי שמעון says:
The sinner's meal offering of כהנים has a handful taken,
and the handful is offered by itself,
and the remainder is offered by itself.
רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says:
The handful is offered by itself,
and the remainder is scattered on the place of the ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about רבי שמעון's view on a כהן's מנחת חוטא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: the קומץ and the שירים are each burned separately. רבי אלעזר: the קומץ is burned and the שירים are scattered on the בית הדשן.

steps.title: Which ash place does רבי אלעזר mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks: if the ash place on top of the מזבח, that is the same as his father's view. If the one below, nothing is ever offered below.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: רבי יוחנן discussed it. Which place of ashes? If the one above, that is his father's view. If the one below, is there anything that is offered below?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks רבי אלעזר's opinion by asking which בית הדשן he means. Both choices seem to cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an ash pile on top of the מזבח and one below it. If רבי אלעזר means the top one, he is saying the same thing as his father, so there is no real disagreement. If he means the bottom one, that makes no sense, because no part of a קרבן is ever offered down there.

keyTerms.meaning: He discussed it, thought it through
Above, on top of the מזבח
Below, under the מזבח
That is the same as his father's view

phrases.english: רבי חייא בר אבא said:
רבי יוחנן discussed it:
The place of ashes, of where?
If the one above, that is his father,
phrases.notes: "His father" means רבי שמעון: if it's the ashes on top of the מזבח, the שירים get burned there, just as he said.

phrases.aramaic: אִי דִּלְמַטָּה – יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁקָּרֵב לְמַטָּה?
phrases.english: If the one below, do you have anything that is offered below?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's opinion from Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר בר רבי שמעון's ruling that the שירים are scattered on the בית הדשן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both choices fail: the upper ash place makes his view the same as his father's, and the lower one is a place where nothing is ever offered.

steps.title: Maybe the שירים are just thrown away
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא suggests that רבי אלעזר means the lower ash place, where the שירים are put just to go to waste.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to him: Perhaps the remainder is scattered there to be wasted?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא tries to save רבי אלעזר's view. Maybe the שירים are not offered below at all, just left there to go to waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the second side of the question. The lower place is not a place of offering, but the שירים could be put there to be destroyed. Then רבי אלעזר really does disagree with his father.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe
To be wasted, to be lost

phrases.english: רבי אבא said to him:
Perhaps to be wasted?
phrases.notes: He means the שירים are scattered on the lower ash pile just to get rid of them, not as an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second side of רבי יוחנן's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the purpose of placing the שירים below: waste, not offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Putting the שירים at the lower ash place would mean offering them below the מזבח, which never happens
steps.terutzMaskana: They are placed there only to be destroyed

steps.title: The חכמים laugh: nothing is offered just to be wasted
steps.stepSummary: The answer is rejected with laughter: no part of a קרבן is ever brought just to be thrown away.
steps.simpleTranslation: They laughed at him: Do you have anything that is offered in order to be wasted?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject רבי אבא's answer by laughing at it. They ask whether any part of the Temple service is done just to waste something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שירים are a holy part of a קרבן, and the חכמים assume no part of a קרבן is ever brought just to be destroyed. So they think the idea of 'to be wasted' does not work. The next step pushes back with a teaching that supports רבי אבא.

keyTerms.meaning: They laughed at him
But really? (a strong question that pushes back)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן asked which בית הדשן רבי אלעזר meant. רבי אבא suggested the שירים are simply wasted, and the חכמים laughed at this. The next step brings a teaching that backs רבי אבא up.

phrases.english: They laughed at him:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁקָּרֵב לְאִיבּוּד?
phrases.english: But do you have anything that is offered to be wasted?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחִיכוּ עֲלֵיהּ, וְכִי יֵשׁ לְךָ דָּבָר שֶׁקָּרֵב לְאִיבּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אבא's answer from Step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that the שירים are placed below just to be wasted
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: No part of a קרבן is ever brought just to be destroyed

steps.title: A teaching showing that a כהן's sin-offering מנחה goes to waste
steps.stepSummary: The father of רבי אבין reads the פסוק as comparing the כהן's מנחה to the חביתין only for not being eaten, not for being fully burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father of רבי אבין taught: 'Every מנחה of a כהן shall be entirely offered, it shall not be eaten.' I compared it only for eating, not for anything else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the laughter of Step 14. It brings a teaching showing that some parts of a קרבן really are left to go to waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק comes right after the כהן גדול's חביתין, which are burned completely. The teaching says a כהן's מנחת חוטא is like the חביתין only in that it is not eaten. It is not like them in being fully burned. So after the קומץ is offered, the rest is neither eaten nor burned, and it simply goes to waste. That supports רבי אבא's reading of רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A meal offering brought by a כהן
Completely burned on the מזבח
I compared it (linked it to another case)
Any other matter

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the teaching says the כהן's מנחת חוטא is burned whole. It is compared to the חביתין ONLY for not being eaten.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rescues רבי אבא's explanation from Step 13. It shows that the תורה itself has a case where leftovers of a קרבן go to waste.

phrases.english: The father of Rabbi Avin taught:
"Every meal offering of a priest shall be entirely offered,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:16. It comes right after the כהן גדול's daily חביתין offering.

phrases.english: it shall not be eaten" –
I compared it for eating,
phrases.notes: He means the כהן's מנחת חוטא is compared to the חביתין: neither one is eaten.

phrases.english: but not for anything else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in Step 14 by showing a case where part of a קרבן is left to waste.
steps.raayaObject: That part of a קרבן can be set aside just to go to waste, which supports רבי אבא's reading of רבי אלעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The father of רבי אבין's reading of ויקרא 6:16.

steps.title: What does this teaching mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the teaching fits the פסוק, since the פסוק plainly says 'entirely offered.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is confused by the teaching and asks for an explanation. This sets up the next steps, where אביי and רבא explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק openly says 'כליל תהיה,' meaning entirely burned. So how can the teaching say the מנחה is NOT like the חביתין in being burned? The גמרא wants to know how the פסוק is being divided.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (a request to explain)

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the teaching in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק can say 'entirely offered' and still teach that the מנחה is not fully burned.

steps.title: אביי splits the פסוק between חובה and נדבה
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the beginning and end of the פסוק together for the חובה, and the middle words for the נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: This is what he means. 'Every מנחה of a כהן... shall not be eaten' is about his obligatory offering. 'Shall be entirely offered' is about his voluntary offering.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. He explains that the פסוק is really talking about two different kinds of מנחה brought by a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חובה (like a מנחת חוטא) is only 'not eaten,' so its leftovers go to waste. The נדבה is 'כליל,' fully burned like the חביתין. To make this work, אביי joins the start of the פסוק to its end and skips the middle words.

keyTerms.meaning: His obligatory offering (like a מנחת חוטא)
His voluntary gift offering
This is what he means

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what he is saying –
"Every meal offering of a priest... shall not be eaten" – that is his obligatory offering,
phrases.notes: The dots show that אביי is skipping the middle words of the פסוק.

phrases.english: "Shall be entirely offered" – that is his gift offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק covers two offerings: the חובה is not eaten (its leftovers are wasted), and the נדבה is fully burned.

steps.title: רבא: that reading chops up the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that אביי's reading cuts the פסוק apart like a sharp knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: A sharp knife is cutting up the verses!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects how אביי divided the פסוק. He does not reject the basic idea of splitting it between חובה and נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי pulled the middle phrase out and glued the start to the end. רבא says that is too forced a way to read a פסוק. He goes after the word order, not the חובה/נדבה idea.

keyTerms.meaning: A sharp knife
Cuts the verses apart

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
A sharp knife is cutting up the verses!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: סַכִּינָא חֲרִיפָא מַפְסְקָא קְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way אביי divided the פסוק in Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only אביי's word order. The חובה/נדבה split itself stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It skips the middle of the פסוק and joins its start to its end, which is a forced reading.

steps.title: רבא's smoother split of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the פסוק in its natural order: the first half is the נדבה and the second half is the חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: 'Every מנחה of a כהן shall be entirely offered' is his voluntary offering. 'It shall not be eaten' is his obligatory offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own reading, which keeps the words of the פסוק in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two halves of the פסוק now line up neatly. The נדבה is fully burned. The חובה is only 'not eaten,' so its leftovers go to waste. The result matches אביי's; only the reading is cleaner.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejecting the earlier answer and giving a new one)

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן's נדבה מנחה is completely burned. His חובה מנחה is not eaten and not fully burned, so its remains go to waste.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
"Every meal offering of a priest shall be entirely offered" – that is his gift offering,
"It shall not be eaten" – that is his obligatory offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's reading, which was rejected in Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the פסוק in its natural order
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Splitting the פסוק requires chopping it up as אביי did.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each half of the פסוק, read in order, covers a different offering.

steps.title: Why not reverse it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the נדבה is the fully burned one rather than the חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I could reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's split. It asks why we should not say the חובה is fully burned and the נדבה is the one wasted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק on its face could fit either order. So the גמרא asks for a reason to give 'כליל' to the נדבה rather than the חובה.

keyTerms.meaning: But I could reverse it

phrases.english: But I could reverse it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges which offering רבא assigned to which half of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's assignment of 'כליל' to the נדבה and 'לא תאכל' to the חובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the פסוק forces this order, so the opposite order should be just as possible.

steps.title: The נדבה is more like the חביתין
steps.stepSummary: The נדבה belongs with 'כליל' because, like the חביתין, it is frequent, comes without a sin, and smells pleasant.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the voluntary offering is the one to include, since it is frequent, it comes without a sin, and its scent is pleasant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It gives three reasons why the נדבה is more like the fully burned חביתין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חביתין are brought often, do not come because of a sin, and have oil and frankincense, which make them fragrant. A כהן's נדבה shares all three traits, but a מנחת חוטא has none of them. So the נדבה is the one that should be fully burned like the חביתין.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it is logical
To include
Frequent, brought often
He did not sin
Its scent is pleasant

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן's נדבה is fully burned like the חביתין because it is like them in three ways: frequent, no sin, and pleasant scent. His חובה is left to waste.

phrases.english: It makes sense that he should include his gift offering,
phrases.notes: He means: include it in 'entirely offered,' together with the חביתין.

phrases.english: since it is frequent,
he did not sin, and its scent is pleasant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'reverse it' challenge of Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A logical argument that the נדבה is more similar to the חביתין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either offering could be the fully burned one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The נדבה matches the חביתין in three ways, so it is the one that is 'כליל.'

steps.title: Maybe the obligatory offering should be included instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the reverse: the priest's obligatory מנחה is more like the חביתין, because it is an עשרון and it is a חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! The פסוק should have included his obligatory offering, because it is a tenth and it is an obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 21. It says the priest's obligatory מנחה also looks like the חביתין, so maybe it belongs with 'כליל' instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 matched the נדבה to the חביתין using three points in common. Here the גמרא offers two points the חובה shares with the חביתין: it is exactly an עשרון, and it is required, not voluntary. If those points count, the חובה could be the one that is fully burned.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite makes more sense
A tenth of an איפה, a fixed measure of flour
An obligatory offering, as opposed to a voluntary one

phrases.english: On the contrary,
it should have included his obligatory offering,
since it is a tenth and an obligation!
phrases.notes: Just like the חביתין, it is exactly a tenth of an איפה, and the כהן has to bring it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of Step 21 by giving rival similarities for the חובה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 21 that the נדבה is the one that matches the חביתין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חובה shares two features with the חביתין (an עשרון and obligatory), so it could just as well be the one called 'כליל'.

steps.title: The gift offering has more points in common
steps.stepSummary: The נדבה's similarities to the חביתין outnumber the חובה's, so the נדבה is the better match.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in two words. The נדבה shares more features with the חביתין than the חובה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נדבה shares three features with the חביתין (frequent, no sin, pleasant smell). The חובה shares only two (an עשרון, obligatory). When comparing, we follow the side with more in common, so רבא's reading stays.

keyTerms.meaning: These, meaning the similarities listed earlier
Are more numerous; there are more of them

steps.whatToRemember: Three similarities beat two. That is why the priest's נדבה, not his חובה, is the מנחה that is fully burned like the חביתין.

phrases.english: These are more numerous.
phrases.notes: The three similarities from Step 21 outweigh the two just mentioned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing similarities: the side with more shared features wins
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חובה's two shared features might make it the match for the חביתין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The נדבה has more shared features, so it is linked to 'כליל'.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from 'לא תאכל'?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that every priest's מנחה is burned whole, so the גמרא asks what they learn from the words 'לא תאכל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: this פסוק, 'Every meal offering of a priest shall be entirely burned; it shall not be eaten', what do they do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the opinion of the רבנן and asks how they use this פסוק. This sets up the next step, which brings a ברייתא as the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, every priest's מנחה is burned completely, so 'כליל' already tells us it is not eaten. That makes 'לא תאכל' look extra. The גמרא wants to know what extra lesson those words teach.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
What do they do with it? How do they use this source?
Entirely; burned whole on the מזבח
It shall not be eaten

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
this verse: "Every meal offering of a priest
shall be entirely burned; it shall not be eaten,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:16

phrases.english: what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי ״כׇּל מִנְחַת כֹּהֵן כָּלִיל תִּהְיֶה לֹא תֵאָכֵל״, מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of how to split the פסוק and asks how the רבנן use it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from the seemingly extra words 'לא תאכל'

steps.title: A ברייתא: each verse states only one rule
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use the פסוק for a ברייתא, which notes that the חביתין is told 'כליל תקטר' and the priest's מנחה is told 'לא תאכל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for what a ברייתא teaches: I would only know that the upper one has 'entirely burned' and the lower one has 'it shall not be eaten'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן need the words for a ברייתא. The ברייתא starts by pointing out that each of the two פסוקים gives only one rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper פסוק (the חביתין) says 'כליל תקטר', and the lower פסוק (the priest's מנחה) says 'לא תאכל'. Read plainly, each offering gets only its own rule. So 'לא תאכל' is not extra. It is one half of a pair that the ברייתא will swap between the offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: They need it for something else
The upper one, the offering in the first פסוק (the חביתין)
The lower one, the offering in the next פסוק (the priest's מנחה)
It shall be entirely burned

phrases.english: They need it for that which is taught in a baraita:
I have only the upper one
phrases.notes: The "upper one" is the חביתין, in the earlier פסוק (ויקרא 6:15).

phrases.english: with "it shall be entirely burned,"
and the lower one with "it shall not be eaten."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 24 by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'לא תאכל' is needed as the rule for the lower offering, which the ברייתא will also apply to the חביתין.

steps.title: How do we swap the rules between the two offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know to apply each offering's rule to the other one.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know to apply what is said of this one to that one, and what is said of that one to this one?
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, a question is asked: how do we know both rules apply to both offerings? This sets up the source given in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is that the חביתין is also 'not eaten' and the priest's מנחה is also 'entirely burned'. The ברייתא wants a source that lets the rules cross over.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? A request for a source

keyTerms.term: לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
keyTerms.meaning: To apply what is said about one case to the other case

phrases.english: From where do we know to apply
what is said of this one to that one,
and what is said of that one to this one?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues by asking for a source to share the two rules.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that both 'כליל' and 'לא תאכל' apply to both offerings

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from the word 'entirely'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers with a גזירה שוה: the word 'כליל' appears in both פסוקים, which links the two offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'entirely' and 'entirely' for a גזירה שוה: 'entirely' is said here, and 'entirely' is said there.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its source. The same word 'כליל' appears for both offerings, and that shared word links them so the rules transfer. The ברייתא keeps going after these words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה connects two passages that use the same word, so a law in one passage also applies in the other. Since both the חביתין and the priest's מנחה are called 'כליל', each receives the other's rule. This is how the רבנן use the words 'לא תאכל'.

keyTerms.meaning: A link between two passages that share the same word, so the law of one applies to the other
Here ... there; the two places being linked

steps.whyThisMatters: This גזירה שוה is how 'לא תאכל' gets a real job for the רבנן: it also forbids eating the חביתין, and 'כליל' also requires burning the priest's מנחה whole.

phrases.english: The verse states "entirely," "entirely,"
for a verbal analogy:
"entirely" is stated here,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the priest's מנחה, and "there" is the חביתין.

phrases.english: and "entirely" is stated there,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word 'כליל', which appears in both פסוקים, transfers each rule to the other offering.

steps.title: Both offerings share both rules
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה gives each offering the other's rule. The חביתין and the priest's מנחה must both be burned whole, and eating either one breaks a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the חביתין is under the rule 'it shall be entirely burned,' so too the priest's מנחה is under that rule. And just as the priest's מנחה has a prohibition against eating it, so too the חביתין has a prohibition against eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out the result of the גזירה שוה on 'כליל' from the previous step. Each offering now takes on the rule that was written only about the other one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חביתין's פסוק says only 'כליל תקטר', and the priest's מנחה's פסוק says only 'לא תאכל'. The shared word 'כליל' links them, so the rules swap over. Now both offerings must be burned whole, and both have a לא תעשה against eating them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Just as there... so too here.' The standard way of carrying a rule from one case to another.
'There.' Here it means the חביתין.
'Here.' Here it means the priest's מנחה.
'To place a negative commandment.' The פסוק is used to make an act forbidden.

steps.whatToRemember: Through the גזירה שוה on 'כליל', both the חביתין and the priest's מנחה must be burned whole, and eating either one breaks a לא תעשה. This is how the רבנן use the words 'לא תאכל'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the answer to step 24. The רבנן do not need 'לא תאכל' to teach that the priest's מנחה is burned whole. They use it to add a prohibition against eating, which then also applies to the חביתין.

phrases.english: Just as there, it is under 'It shall be entirely burned,'
phrases.notes: 'There' is the חביתין and 'here' is the priest's מנחה, the two offerings linked in the last step.

phrases.english: so too here, it is under 'It shall be entirely burned.'

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה כָּאן לִיתֵּן לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה עַל אֲכִילָתוֹ,
phrases.english: And just as here, the פסוק comes to place a prohibition on eating it,

phrases.aramaic: אַף לְהַלָּן לִיתֵּן לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה עַל אֲכִילָתוֹ.
phrases.english: so too there, it comes to place a prohibition on eating it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַלָּן בְּ״כָלִיל תׇּקְטָר״, אַף כָּאן בְּ״כָלִיל תׇּקְטָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the result of the גזירה שוה given in step 27.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חביתין and the priest's מנחה are each burned whole, and each is forbidden to be eaten under a לא תעשה.

steps.title: A priest who eats from the altar portions
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks what the law is for a כהן who eats from the אימורין. He begins by mentioning the prohibition of זרות, and his question continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא asks: if a כהן ate from the parts of an offering meant for the altar, what is the law? The prohibition about a non-priest eating...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. רבינא asks about a כהן who eats from the אימורין, the parts of an offering that are burned on the altar. The sentence keeps going in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic of 'not eating altar food' raises a new case. Normally the לאו of זרות is about a non-priest eating holy food. Here the eater is a כהן, so רבינא is starting to work out which prohibition, if any, he breaks.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He asks.' Introduces a real question whose answer is not yet known.
The parts of an animal offering that are burned on the altar.
'What is it?' meaning 'What is the law?'
The prohibition against a non-priest (זר) eating holy food.
